newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL IPO PRICING MAY 6, OFFERING MAY 9-APV. [CORRECTED 09:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: MOL IPO PRICING MAY 6, OFFERING MAY 9-APV. [CORRECTED 09:05 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects date of share pricing in headline and text from May 2 to May 6.)

Hungary will offer at least 12.5 percent of the shares in oil and gas company MOL to international institutional investors and a minimum of one percent to domestic investors, the state privatisation agency APV said on Thursday.

For the global offering, APV granted the joint global co-ordinators -- Dresdner Kleinwort Benson and Salomon Brothers International -- an over-allotment option on a further 2.5 percent in MOL, APV said in a statement.
APV plans to hold an international roadshow in Europe, Asia, the Middle East and in North America between April 21 and May 2, and to price and allocate the shares on May 6.

The offering to Hungarian institutional and retail investors is expected to begin on May 9, on the condition that Hungary's securities market watchdog approves the prospectus of the domestic offering.
If demand for the shares in Hungary is larger than the offered amount, a further one percent stake will be sold domestically, APV said.
Domestic retail investors will be allowed to subscribe the shares in cash instalments, paying 30 percent of the price at the subscription and the remaining part by 15 May, 1998.
All shares to be offered globally and domestically will bear the right for dividend on MOL's 1996 results.
MOL Rt had 1996 net income of 22.2 billion HUF, a sharp rise from 1.1 billion in 1995.
MOL's registered capital is 98.4 billion forints.
